_comment: Network-delay experiment, clean re-implementation. This config is
separate from configs/commcost.json: run it with `runner matrix --config
configs/networkdelay.json --results-base network_delay_clean`, which
writes to results/network_delay_clean/.
The delay is applied OUTSIDE the implementations: the runner installs a
tc/netem qdisc inside each replica's own network namespace, identically
for every implementation. No adapter sleeps, no application-level jitter,
and no consensus source is modified, so the condition a run is measured
under is not produced by the code under test.
Traffic scope is filter=peers: only packets addressed to another replica
are delayed, so client-observed request latency is not polluted by an
emulation the consensus path alone should receive. Every replica delays
its own egress, so an inter-replica round trip accumulates the configured
one-way delay once per hop.
There is no jitter: jitter is removed from the main experiment. The
archived results/commcost/ family used in-adapter sleeps WITH jitter and
is treated as a separate legacy dataset - it is never pooled with these
delay-only results and never reinterpreted as one another (labcfg.Validate
also refuses a run that sets both mechanisms).
The `defaults` block is a verbatim copy of configs/matrix.json's defaults
(same CPU/memory allocation, keyspace, timeouts, Raft timeouts, seed and
10 repetitions), so only the network condition differs.
Expected cost per point: the client timeout is 2000 ms, so at 10 ms
one-way (20 ms per consensus round trip) a protocol whose path needs many
sequential round trips is expected to lose requests to timeouts. Those
timeouts are a property of the configured timeout, not of the protocol,
and are reported as such.
